field_commentary.value: 西行の庵は多数知られているが、小倉に庵があったことは、『山家集』に「小倉の麓に住みけるに鹿の鳴きけるを聞きて」の詞書（436番歌）や、「我がものと/秋の梢を思うかな/小倉の里に/家居せしより」（486番歌）とあることより推定され、現在、小倉山二尊院に西行法師庵跡の石碑がある。しかし、この能の舞台は、京都西方一帯の山を意味する「西山」にある西行の安室としか書かれていない。西山のどこかにあった西行の庵から見える小倉山の桜を描写したものかもしれない。

field_commentary_eng.value: There are several huts of Saigyō (Saigyō an) known. The one in Ogura is conjectured on the basis of the preface to poem no. 436 in Saigyō’s Sankashū “When he was living on the peak of Ogura he heard deer bellowing” and poem no. 486 “I think of the tree tops in autumn as my own since I have come to live in the village of Ogura”. Today, there is a stone monument in Nison temple at Ogura yama on the place Saigyō’s hut is supposed to have stood. However, the scene of this nō piece is just given as the quite hut of Saigyō in "Nishi yama" which refers to the mountains in the west of Kyōto in general. Perhaps it is the image of the cherry blossoms at Ogura yama seen from the hut of Saigyō situated somewhere in the mountains in the west.

Today, there is a stone monument in Nison temple at Ogura yama on the place Saigyō’s hut is supposed to have stood. However, the scene of this nō piece is just given as the quite hut of Saigyō in "Nishi yama" which refers to the mountains in the west of Kyōto in general. field_scene_description.value: 花見の客が群がるのは、桜の罪だと歌った西行法師（ワキ）のもとに、白髪の老人（シテ、実は桜の精）が現れ、罪は有情の人にあり、非情の桜の罪ではないと諭したあと、桜の名所を謡い、舞に興じるうち、夜があけてきた場面。桜の精は、白んで見えるのは、小倉山に残る夜桜の花だと、花見の時が終わるのを惜しんでいる。

field_scene_description_eng.value: An old man with white hair (shite, in reality the spirit of the cherry trees) appears in front of the monk Saigyō (waki) who is known for having composed a poem putting the blame for people gathering for hanami on the cherry blossoms. The old man explains that sin can only be attributed to beings with emotions, and the gatherings are not the fault of the cherry blossoms that are devoid of emotions. While he sings of the famous site for cherry blossoms and performs a dance, it begins to dawn. The spirit of the cherry blossoms is deploring the end of hanami as there are only the night blossoms left on Ogura yama shining white.

ワキ「昨日は薄きもみぢ葉の。

シテ「今日は濃染の色深き。

ワキ「西紅の峯つづき。

シテ「さながら四方の。

二人「錦なれども。

field_commentary_eng.value: The Yōkyoku taikan comments that Ogura yama is compared here to Aone ga mine, but as Ogura yama is a famous site for autumn leaves, green (ao) does not match. Ogura yama is cited probably for its image as a famous place for autumn leaves.

grass blankets the fields

spearheads dimly visible

this dusky autumn evening”

field_scene_description_eng.value: A person from Yoshino (waki) goes to the Dainenbutsu (Buddhist memorial service) at Seiryō-ji Temple in Sagano, with a child (kokata), whom he had picked up around Saidai-ji Temple in Nara. There they meet a mad woman called Hyakuman (shite). The child says that this mad woman must be the mother from whom he was separated, and as the person from Yoshino talks to her, she tells them how she arrived at Seiryō-ji Temple from Nara in search of her child.

field_commentary.value: 嵯峨野から樒が原に行く途中に小倉があり、その経由地として、名所の小倉があげられている。樒が原は、愛宕山の西麓にあった野で歌枕。『堀河百首』冬「時雨つつ/ 日数はふとも/ あたご山/ しきみか原の/ 色はかはらじ」(藤原顕仲)などに詠まれる。旧地名は、葛野郡嵯峨町原。

field_commentary_eng.value:
On the way from Sagano to Shikimigahara there lies Ogura, a famous place, which is mentioned as a transit point. Shikimigahara is a field at the western foot of Atago-yama and used as utamakura (a famous place with a poetic association). It is mentioned in Horikawa hyakushu (Hundred Poems during the reign of Emperor Horikawa) in the section winter poems:

“Even though rain in winter keeps drizzling for days, the colour of Atago-yama and Shikimigahara doesn’t change” (by Fujiwara no Akinaka)

The former name of the area was Kazurano-gun Saga Machibara.

<p>On the way from Sagano to Shikimigahara there lies Ogura, a famous place, which is mentioned as a transit point. It is mentioned in<em> Horikawa hyakushu</em> (Hundred Poems during the reign of Emperor Horikawa) in the section winter poems:</p>
<p>“Even though rain in winter keeps drizzling for days, the colour of Atago-yama and Shikimigahara doesn’t change” (by Fujiwara no Akinaka)</p>
<p>The former name of the area was Kazurano-gun Saga Machibara.</p>
